name: OpenVLA-OFT
summary: A systematic study of VLA fine-tuning design choices. Replacing autoregressive token-by-token decoding with a single parallel forward pass, predicting a whole action chunk at once, and regressing continuous actions with an L1 objective instead of classifying bins lifted throughput from ~5 Hz to over 100 Hz while raising success rates, including on bimanual tasks the original model could not perform.
innovation: Parallel decoding of an entire action chunk in one forward pass, removing the autoregressive bottleneck.
Continuous L1 regression head shown to match diffusion heads at a fraction of inference cost.
FiLM language conditioning to stop the model ignoring instructions in multi-task settings.
matters: Turned VLAs from demo-speed into control-rate systems; the recipe was widely adopted.
limits: An adaptation recipe, not a new pretrained model, so it inherits OpenVLA's pretraining ceiling.
lineage: A direct engineering upgrade of OpenVLA's decoding and action representation.
